messages:
Alex: quick heads up — master@a1b2c3 deploy bumped tail latency ~12% on kv-lookup path, suspect kernel handoff to small-batch kernel. :eyes:
Maya: where in the trace? can you paste the nsys command you used? :magnifying_glass:
Alex: here's the short capture I ran (10s) — useful to reproduce the tail: 
```bash
nsys profile -o kv-handoff --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=cpu --sample-interval=1ms --duration=10s --capture-range=nvtx -- ./bin/infer --profile-mode
```
Maya: good start. also add NVTX spans around the batching and KV boundaries so capture-range picks logical ops.
Alex: added NVTX like this inline in the runner: 
```python
import torch
from torch.cuda import nvtx
with nvtx.range("batcher:request-{{id}}"):
    with nvtx.range("kv:lookup"):
        model.step(request)
```
Sam: fyi we've seen the same pattern before — the heuristic that splits >8 tokens sometimes falls back to `attn_small_batch` kernel. that kernel has worse per-token throughput for short sequences.
Alex: timeline shows alternating `attn_large` and `attn_small_batch` inside the same request span. with sample-interval=1ms we catch the larger kernels but miss many tiny handoffs. bumping sampling to 200us made the tiny spikes visible.
perfbot: analysis ready — hotspot summary uploaded: s3://perf/kv-handoff/2140534444/summary.html (includes kernel timeline + top kernels).
Maya: another hypothesis — KV cache thrash after the sharding change last week. NVTX tags on KV read/write will let us correlate evictions with kernel switches.
Sam: also try a focused capture: drop nvtx for a clean cuda+osrt trace to reduce noise, then do a separate nvtx-scoped run for ranges. both are useful.
Alex: quick log snippet from the re-run with 200us sampling: 
```
[TRACE] req=0x7f9a kv:read start
[kernel] attn_large   1.8ms  (seq=64)
[kernel] attn_small_batch  0.35ms  (seq=8)
[kernel] attn_small_batch  0.38ms  (seq=6)
[TRACE] req=0x7f9a kv:read end
[kernel] attn_large  1.9ms (next chunk)
```
Alex: seems like the batching heuristic splits and then subsequent KV read pushes cache state leading to extra small kernels.
Maya: actions: add NVTX to both batcher and kv ops, re-run with --sample-interval=200us for 15s, and capture a single slow request with --target-pid so we get full request timeline.
Sam: add a perf CI check that simulates short-seq traffic and asserts we don't flip to `attn_small_batch` more than X% during steady state.
Alex: running the 15s capture now, will drop the link and flame image when done. Thanks! :thumbsup:
